#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding()]
param()

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
. (Join-Path $scriptDir 'plugin-env.ps1')
. (Join-Path $scriptDir 'resolve-cache-dir.ps1')

$cacheDir = Resolve-McpCacheDir
$sessionFile = Join-Path $cacheDir 'session-state.yaml'
$turnFile = Join-Path $cacheDir 'current-turn.yaml'
$pendingDir = Join-Path $cacheDir 'pending'
$namespaces = @(
    'workflow.sessionlog'
    'workflow.todo'
    'workflow.requirements'
    'workflow.triage'
    'workflow.graphrag'
    'workflow.memory'
    'workflow.failsafe'
)
$requirementMethods = @(
    'workflow.requirements.listLayers'
    'workflow.requirements.createLayer'
    'workflow.requirements.updateLayer'
    'workflow.requirements.effective'
    'workflow.requirements.planRecovery'
    'workflow.requirements.applyRecovery'
    'workflow.requirements.getRecovery'
)
$requirementClientMethods = @(
    'client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync'
    'client.Requirements.CreateRequirementLayerAsync'
    'client.Requirements.UpdateRequirementLayerAsync'
    'client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync'
    'client.Requirements.PlanRecoveryAsync'
    'client.Requirements.ApplyRecoveryAsync'
    'client.Requirements.GetRecoveryAsync'
)

function Test-McpStatusSessionState {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)

    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return $false }

    try {
        $statusLine = Select-String -LiteralPath $Path -Pattern '^status:\s*verified\s*$' | Select-Object -First 1
        if (-not $statusLine) { return $false }

        $sessionLine = Select-String -LiteralPath $Path -Pattern '^sessionId:\s*(?<value>.+)$' | Select-Object -First 1
        if (-not $sessionLine) { return $false }

        $sessionId = [string]$sessionLine.Matches[0].Groups['value'].Value
        $sessionId = $sessionId.Trim().Trim('''').Trim('"')
        return -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($sessionId)
    } catch {
        return $false

[CmdletBinding()]
param(

)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

function Get-JUnitCase {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)
    [xml]$doc = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Raw
    $cases = @($doc.SelectNodes('//testcase'))
    $failed = @($cases | Where-Object { $_.SelectSingleNode('failure') -or $_.SelectSingleNode('error') }).Count
    $skipped = @($cases | Where-Object { $_.SelectSingleNode('skipped') }).Count
    $names = @($cases | ForEach-Object { '{0} :: {1}' -f $_.GetAttribute('classname'), $_.GetAttribute('name') })
    $suites = @($doc.SelectNodes('//testsuite') | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('timestamp') } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object)
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Count        = $cases.Count
        Failed       = $failed
        Skipped      = $skipped
        Names        = $names
        FirstSuiteTs = if ($suites.Count) { $suites[0] } else { '' }
        LastSuiteTs  = if ($suites.Count) { $suites[-1] } else { '' }
    }
}

function Get-TrxCase {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)
    [xml]$doc = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Raw
    $ns = New-Object System.Xml.XmlNamespaceManager($doc.NameTable)
    $ns.AddNamespace('t', 'http://microsoft.com/schemas/VisualStudio/TeamTest/2010')
    $results = @($doc.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTestResult', $ns))
    $outcomes = $results | Group-Object { $_.GetAttribute('outcome') } | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.Name, $_.Count }
    $counters = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:ResultSummary/t:Counters', $ns)
    $times = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:Times', $ns)
    $defs = @($doc.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTest', $ns))
    $names = @($defs | ForEach-Object {
            $tm = $_.SelectSingleNode('t:TestMethod', $ns)
            '{0} :: {1}' -f $tm.GetAttribute('className'), $tm.GetAttribute('name')
        })
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Count    = $results.Count
        Outcomes = ($outcomes -join ',')
        Counters = if ($counters) { ($counters.Attributes | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.Name, $_.Value }) -join ',' } else { '' }
        Times    = if ($times) { ($times.Attributes | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.Name, $_.Value }) -join ',' } else { '' }
        Names    = $names
    }
}

$index = Get-Content -LiteralPath $IndexPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
'INDEX revision=' + $index.revision + ' timestamp=' + $index.timestamp
$manifestHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $index.sourceManifest -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
'MANIFEST sha256 match=' + ($manifestHash -eq $index.sourceManifestSha256) + ' actual=' + $manifestHash
foreach ($r in $index.reports) {
    $jh = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $r.junit -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $th = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $r.trx -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $j = Get-JUnitCase -Path $r.junit
    $t = Get-TrxCase -Path $r.trx
    $jSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$j.Names)
    $tSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$t.Names)
    $onlyJ = @($j.Names | Where-Object { -not $tSet.Contains($_) })
    $onlyT = @($t.Names | Where-Object { -not $jSet.Contains($_) })
    $dupJ = @($j.Names | Group-Object | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object Name)
    [pscustomobject]@{
        name           = $r.name
        junitHashMatch = ($jh -eq $r.junitSha256)
        trxHashMatch   = ($th -eq $r.trxSha256)
        indexCases     = $r.cases
        junitCases     = $j.Count
        junitFailed    = $j.Failed
        junitSkipped   = $j.Skipped
        junitFirstTs   = $j.FirstSuiteTs
        junitLastTs    = $j.LastSuiteTs
        trxCases       = $t.Count
        trxOutcomes    = $t.Outcomes
        trxCounters    = $t.Counters
        trxTimes       = $t.Times
        onlyInJUnit    = $onlyJ.Count
        onlyInTrx      = $onlyT.Count
        duplicateNames = $dupJ.Count
        junitWrite     = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $r.junit).LastWriteTime.ToString('s')
        trxWrite       = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $r.trx).LastWriteTime.ToString('s')
    } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
}

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$ReportDirectory)
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
$root=(Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../..')).ProviderPath
$test=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.Tests.ps1'
$correct=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockCorrect.psm1'
$wrong=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockWrong.psm1'
$wrongEmpty=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockWrongEmpty.psm1'
if(-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($ReportDirectory,'Run independent planner mock gate and save evidence')){return}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ReportDirectory -Force|Out-Null
$runs=@()
foreach($case in @(@{name='correct';module=$correct},@{name='wrong';module=$wrong},@{name='wrong-empty';module=$wrongEmpty})){
    $env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE=$case.module
    $configuration=New-PesterConfiguration
    $configuration.Run.Path=@($test)
    $configuration.Run.PassThru=$true
    $configuration.Output.Verbosity='Detailed'
    $configuration.TestResult.Enabled=$true
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputFormat='NUnitXml'
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputPath=Join-Path $ReportDirectory ($case.name+'.xml')
    $result=Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration
    $cases=@($result.Tests | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{name=$_.Name;result=[string]$_.Result} })
    $runs+= [pscustomobject]@{name=$case.name;passed=$result.PassedCount;failed=$result.FailedCount;skipped=$result.SkippedCount;cases=$cases}
}
Remove-Item Env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if($runs[0].passed -ne 6 -or $runs[0].failed -ne 0 -or $runs[0].skipped -ne 0){throw 'Correct mock did not pass every planner case.'}
foreach($case in $runs[0].cases){
    $controls=@($runs[1..2] | ForEach-Object { $_.cases | Where-Object name -CEQ $case.name })
    if($controls.Count -ne 2 -or @($controls | Where-Object result -EQ 'Failed').Count -eq 0){throw "No rejecting negative control for: $($case.name)"}
}
$receipt=[pscustomobject]@{
    timestamp=Get-Date -Format s
    root=$root
    test=(Resolve-Path $test).ProviderPath
    testSha256=(Get-FileHash $test -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    correctMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $correct -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    wrongMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $wrong -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    wrongEmptyMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $wrongEmpty -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    runs=$runs
    qualification='Catch-up mock sensitivity check. This receipt does not backdate or replace the original pre-implementation gate.'
}
$receipt|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6|Set-Content (Join-Path $ReportDirectory 'mock-gate.json')

1	# Guest game and GitHub admin PWA release
2	
3	Current operator scope, 28 October 2026. This document supersedes the public
4	OpenAI sign-in, public PWA installation and browser role-delegation portions of
5	the earlier designs. QBrain is authoritative; this is its linked implementation
6	and verification projection. Implementation and hosted rollout are in progress.
7	
8	## Behavior and boundaries
9	
10	The public game accepts guests only. Generated aliases, icons, browser-persistent
11	guest credentials, rooms, private live updates and reactions remain available.
12	Public OpenAI login/callback routes return404. Public session responses expose no
13	administration permissions, stored/bootstrap grants do not elevate guests, and
14	member-shaped public sessions are rejected. Community suggestion/nomination UI
15	and the former `/content` entry are inactive in this release.
16	
17	Administration uses the registered [Word Pairs Admin GitHub App](https://github.com/settings/apps/word-pairs-admin-sharpninja).
18	Only verified GitHub numeric account16146732 and login `sharpninja` can complete
19	sign-in. The private App requests no repository, organization or email permissions
20	and has no webhook. User-access delegation is disabled: `/admin/users` redirects
21	to `/admin` and its API returns404 without touching access storage. Existing ACL
22	and community policy/domain/history remain preserved for future scope.
23	
24	Server configuration uses `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and
25	`WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, never public-prefixed variables. Both callback
26	URLs are registered exactly:
27	
28	- `https://wordpairs.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (staging).
29	- `https://wordpairs-j9jf.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (production).
30	
31	The provider uses Authorization Code with S256PKCE and state. Existing persisted
32	challenges are browser-bound, expire after10minutes and are consumed before
33	callback validation. The server exchanges the code and verifies `/user`; it
34	retains neither GitHub access/refresh tokens nor provider email. Admin cookies
35	`wp_admin`/`wp_admin_login` and stored hashes have a separate `github-admin` purpose
36	namespace from `wp_session`. Copying a guest token into an admin cookie or the
37	reverse cannot authenticate. Admin login/logout leaves the guest session intact.
38	Admin responses are private/no-store; logout requires the canonical same origin.
39	
40	## Installation and offline behavior
41	
42	Only the admin layout links `/admin/manifest.webmanifest`. Its stable identity,
43	start URL and scope are `/admin`; display is standalone and its name is Wordpairs
44	Admin. Existing opaque192/512 PNGs, maskable icon and Apple touch icon are reused.
45	The manifest is an explicit route because nested `admin/manifest.ts` is not a
46	recognized metadata convention in the installed Next.js version.
47	
48	Authenticated admin UI offers installation and phone instructions. It registers
49	`/admin-sw.js` with scope `/admin`, `updateViaCache: none`, no-store script headers
50	and `Service-Worker-Allowed: /admin`. The worker handles only same-origin GET
51	admin document navigation. HTTP errors pass through; a network failure receives
52	the generic `/admin-offline.html` reconnect/sign-in screen. API/auth/RSC requests,
53	mutations and public game navigation receive no offline fallback. No operation
54	is queued for later execution.
55	
56	Only the offline document and four public icons are cached under
57	`wordpairs-admin-pwa-v1`. Sessions, profiles, admin HTML, answers, room projections,
58	credentials and mutation responses are never put in CacheStorage. Normal admin
59	updates wait for active clients and delete only older admin cache versions.
60	
61	Public pages have no manifest or install controls. The former `/sw.js` remains
62	as a retirement worker with no fetch handler; it deletes only `wordpairs-pwa-*`
63	caches and unregisters itself. Root cleanup recognizes only that exact former
64	root registration and cache prefix, preserving admin and unrelated apps. Website
65	code cannot remove an existing OS home-screen icon or prevent browser bookmarks.
66	
67	## Traceability and repeatable cases
68	
69	QBrain records: `FR-GUESTADMIN-031`, `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043`,
70	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149`; updated existing `FR-IDENTITY-018`,
71	`FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002`, `FR-ADMINPAGES-023`, `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026`,
72	`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
73	`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
74	`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
75	preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
76	and independent review justify a separate status update.
77	
78	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
79	  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
80	  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
81	  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
82	  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
83	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
84	  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
85	  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
86	  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
87	  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
88	  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
89	  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
90	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to
91	  `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`: inspect actual production HTML/manifest/icons; await real
92	  worker activation; inspect unfiltered Chromium installability diagnostics using
93	  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.
94	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-06..09`, `TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037` and
95	  `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-05..07` map to `TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138`: inspect the actual
96	  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
97	  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
98	  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
99	  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
100	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
101	 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
102	  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.
103	
104	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
105	administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
106	session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
107	adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
108	Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
109	opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
110	Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
111	matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.
112	
113	Ordered actions and expected observations:
114	
115	1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
116	   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
117	   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
118	2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
119	   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
120	   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
121	3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
122	   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
123	   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
124	4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
125	   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
126	   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
127	5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
128	   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
129	   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.
130	
131	Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
132	contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
133	contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
134	ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
135	not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.
136	
137	The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
138	network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
139	checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
140	The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
141	it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
142	[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).
143	
144	```gherkin
145	Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
146	  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
147	  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
148	  Then no administrator profile is returned
149	  And no private catalog records are read
150	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
151	  Then the callback creates no administrator session
152	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
153	  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
154	  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
155	  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
156	  When the administrator signs out
157	  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
158	  And the guest session remains usable
159	```
160	
161	## Verification, operations and open dependencies
162	
163	Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser
164	`npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts`. The full active browser
165	suite includes all currently enabled guest/game/admin flows. Source-level provider
166	and namespace tests are `tests/integration/github-admin.test.ts` and
167	`tests/integration/admin-session-isolation.test.ts`; HTTP checks include
168	`tests/web/github-admin-api.test.ts`. The hostile-review correction adds forward
169	migration `012_guest_public_profiles.sql`; no package is added. Existing schema
170	and private Realtime/scheduler remain separate deployment prerequisites.
171	
172	Real PostgreSQL coverage in `tests/integration/admin.integration.ts` exercises the
173	actual login/callback/session/content routes and runtime composition, with only
174	the external GitHub transport faked. It verifies stored one-time challenges,
175	cross-realm denial, catalog writes, callback replay and durable logout. Run the
176	full database suite with `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1 -ReportDirectory <path>`;
177	`-VolatileStorage` uses an owned temporary PostgreSQL container and does not prove
178	disk durability or crash recovery. `scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1` adapts each
179	native JUnit case into the review's TRX format, preserving original JUnit receipts.
180	TRX conversion timestamps are explicitly distinguished from execution times.
181	
182	The wider browser run also exposed a presence-timer regression:15-second profile
183	refreshes changed the profile object and restarted the20-second heartbeat effect.
184	Room refresh now depends on stable profile ID; the existing uncertain-readiness
185	browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
186	now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
187	desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.
188	
189	Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
190	OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.
191	The first architecture review rejected a nested manifest and missing callback
192	feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is
193	Claude Opus, explicitly selected by the operator. Real hosted GitHub consent,
194	standalone phone OAuth cookie continuity and physical OS installation remain
195	distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
196	name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.
197	
198	## Hostile-review recovery slice
199	
200	Claude Opus round1 rejected candidate437c501 at92%accuracy/88%completeness.
201	Its full findings and persistence proof are retained under `docs/receipts/hv/`.
202	The owner was created with the former member public-default, without a public
203	preferences route. The earlier PostgreSQL public-read failure exposed the extra
204	row; fixture cleanup made the suite independent but did not repair that product
205	privacy problem. That distinction was missing from the original failure analysis.
206	
207	The operator confirmed: "Hide all old member profiles". GA-10 therefore requires
208	new members to default private and all member identities, including retired
209	OpenAI records, to be excluded by the server's public query even if their stored
210	flag remains true. Preserve historical records, guest opt-in, ranking, paging and
211	revision conflicts. Add a forward SQL migration after the existing hosted history;
212	apply it to staging first, verify, then production. No data deletion or provider
213	token import is needed. Existing cached public pages may expire over their normal
214	five-minute read lifetime; restart/deployment creates fresh application caches.
215	
216	Before this correction, the independent GA-10 oracle accepted a private member
217	and guest-only rows, and rejected a public member and both owner/legacy leaks.
218	The mock gate passed3/3 at20:22:38 on28October2026. The same oracle is bound to
219	the real identity service and PostgreSQL query. This is evidence for the recovery
220	slice, not a reconstruction of the missing original pre-implementation gate.
221	The original slice's chronological process receipt remains missing and is not
222	claimed satisfied. On28October2026 the operator explicitly answered "Record the
223	one-time exception" to question `call_30e2a1f3011842979ab422d87f21432e`. This is a
224	one-time exception for that historical missing receipt only. It does not waive
225	fresh hostile validation, current tests, security checks, migration verification
226	or hosted observations. No original chronology is reconstructed. The decision
227	and QBrain readback are retained in `docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/process-exception.json`.
228	All current status/criteria remain in progress/unsatisfied.
229	
230	Recovery work also supplies explicit GA-05/06/07 cross-references to canonical
231	PWA criteria and their TEST/TR records, GA-09 on the responsive TR/admin TEST,
232	reproducible adapter fixtures and full post-edit PWA browser execution. No prior
233	failed review or test receipt is removed. Fresh review follows the full applicable
234	unit, PostgreSQL, browser, lint and production-build checks.
235	
236	Claude Opus round2 rejected the corrective candidate at95%accuracy and
237	94%completeness. Its four FAILs were a missing mock-first gate for the deployment
238	planner edit, continued extension of a Node script tool, an incomplete candidate
239	source hash manifest, and missing pre-run analyzer receipts for the JUnit/TRX
240	adapter scripts. The full verdict and request/response receipts remain under
241	`docs/receipts/hv/`. None of the four findings is represented as resolved by a
242	reviewer yet.
243	
244	For the next review, a PowerShell schema planner and CLI replace the Node planner.
245	The planner's six contract cases were written and run against correct and
246	intentionally wrong mocks before the PowerShell implementation. Their original
247	JUnit, mock-gate summary, real-run JUnit and adapted TRX receipts are in
248	`docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/planner-*`. The tracked source-manifest
249	generator enumerates literal Git paths, including bracketed routes, public assets
250	and root test/build configuration; its current path-set check covers276 files.
251	The adapter analyzer receipt records parser and ScriptAnalyzer results for both
252	scripts before the fresh three-fixture run. These are local process receipts, not
253	approval to deploy. The final source manifest and all execution reports must be
254	regenerated against the frozen source revision that the next hostile review sees.
255

Administration uses the registered [Word Pairs Admin GitHub App](https://github.com/settings/apps/word-pairs-admin-sharpninja).
Only verified GitHub numeric account16146732 and login `sharpninja` can complete
sign-in. The private App requests no repository, organization or email permissions
and has no webhook. User-access delegation is disabled: `/admin/users` redirects
to `/admin` and its API returns404 without touching access storage. Existing ACL
and community policy/domain/history remain preserved for future scope.

Server configuration uses `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and
`WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, never public-prefixed variables. Both callback
URLs are registered exactly:

- `https://wordpairs.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (staging).
- `https://wordpairs-j9jf.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (production).

The provider uses Authorization Code with S256PKCE and state. Existing persisted
challenges are browser-bound, expire after10minutes and are consumed before
callback validation. The server exchanges the code and verifies `/user`; it
retains neither GitHub access/refresh tokens nor provider email. Admin cookies
`wp_admin`/`wp_admin_login` and stored hashes have a separate `github-admin` purpose
namespace from `wp_session`. Copying a guest token into an admin cookie or the
reverse cannot authenticate. Admin login/logout leaves the guest session intact.
Admin responses are private/no-store; logout requires the canonical same origin.

## Installation and offline behavior

Only the admin layout links `/admin/manifest.webmanifest`. Its stable identity,
start URL and scope are `/admin`; display is standalone and its name is Wordpairs
Admin. Existing opaque192/512 PNGs, maskable icon and Apple touch icon are reused.
The manifest is an explicit route because nested `admin/manifest.ts` is not a
recognized metadata convention in the installed Next.js version.

Authenticated admin UI offers installation and phone instructions. It registers
`/admin-sw.js` with scope `/admin`, `updateViaCache: none`, no-store script headers
and `Service-Worker-Allowed: /admin`. The worker handles only same-origin GET
admin document navigation. HTTP errors pass through; a network failure receives
the generic `/admin-offline.html` reconnect/sign-in screen. API/auth/RSC requests,
mutations and public game navigation receive no offline fallback. No operation
is queued for later execution.

Only the offline document and four public icons are cached under
`wordpairs-admin-pwa-v1`. Sessions, profiles, admin HTML, answers, room projections,
credentials and mutation responses are never put in CacheStorage. Normal admin
updates wait for active clients and delete only older admin cache versions.

Public pages have no manifest or install controls. The former `/sw.js` remains
as a retirement worker with no fetch handler; it deletes only `wordpairs-pwa-*`
caches and unregisters itself. Root cleanup recognizes only that exact former
root registration and cache prefix, preserving admin and unrelated apps. Website
code cannot remove an existing OS home-screen icon or prevent browser bookmarks.

## Traceability and repeatable cases

QBrain records: `FR-GUESTADMIN-031`, `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043`,
`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149`; updated existing `FR-IDENTITY-018`,
`FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002`, `FR-ADMINPAGES-023`, `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026`,
`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
and independent review justify a separate status update.

- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to

  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.

  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.

`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.

Ordered actions and expected observations:

1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.

Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.

The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).

```gherkin
Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
  Then no administrator profile is returned
  And no private catalog records are read
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
  Then the callback creates no administrator session
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
  When the administrator signs out
  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
  And the guest session remains usable
```

## Verification, operations and open dependencies

Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser

browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.

Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.

feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is

distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.

privacy problem. That distinction was missing from the original failure analysis.

new members to default private and all member identities, including retired

flag remains true. Preserve historical records, guest opt-in, ranking, paging and

token import is needed. Existing cached public pages may expire over their normal

and guest-only rows, and rejected a public member and both owner/legacy leaks.
The mock gate passed3/3 at20:22:38 on28October2026. The same oracle is bound to

failed review or test receipt is removed. Fresh review follows the full applicable

94%completeness. Its four FAILs were a missing mock-first gate for the deployment
planner edit, continued extension of a Node script tool, an incomplete candidate
source hash manifest, and missing pre-run analyzer receipts for the JUnit/TRX
adapter scripts. The full verdict and request/response receipts remain under
`docs/receipts/hv/`. None of the four findings is represented as resolved by a
reviewer yet.

intentionally wrong mocks before the PowerShell implementation. Their original
JUnit, mock-gate summary, real-run JUnit and adapted TRX receipts are in

28	This document defines how Wordpairs will be provisioned, built, deployed, operated, rolled back, and released under the project's current constraints. 34	## 2.1 TR-only verification, separate from AC coverage
35	
36	The following contract tests are specified before implementation and validated against mocks before the corresponding scripts/build code is written. They do not add ACs or count toward AC coverage. Real Vercel, Supabase, and deployment checks run later as technical integration evidence.

42	| TR-22 | `TR-22-T01`: application ports handle repository/Realtime success, failure, retry, and stale-state responses without assuming process memory is durable. | Disposable Supabase integration verifies persistence, RLS, transactions, and Realtime behavior. |

48	## 2. Deployment principles and constraints
49	
50	1. **No paid usage:** keep Vercel on Hobby and Supabase on Free. Never add a card-backed resource, paid add-on, metered service, or automatic paid fallback. A quota error is a recoverable application state, not permission to spend.
51	2. **Hobby is personal/non-commercial:** Vercel documents Hobby as personal, non-commercial use. Confirm continued eligibility before launch and whenever the project's use changes. If use becomes commercial, this deployment target no longer satisfies the requirement; stop and revise the hosting decision before continuing.
52	3. **Repository and author requirements:** the repo is public under the `sharpninja` account. Keep Vercel connected to the matching personal Git provider account. Vercel's current Hobby Git rules require the commit author to own the destination Hobby team; verify this on the first deployment and after changing Git identities. Private repositories in GitHub organizations are not deployable to Hobby under current Vercel rules.
53	4. **Environment separation:** local Development, Vercel Preview/Staging, and Vercel Production must use distinct secrets and data. Never pass Production credentials to a Preview deployment.
54	5. **Git is the deployment trigger:** pushes to non-production branches produce Preview deployments; pushes/merges to `main` produce Production deployments. Do not add a second deploy trigger that can race or bypass the approved path.
55	6. **Migrations are versioned:** schema changes live in reviewed migration files. No manual dashboard schema edits in a hosted environment; make any emergency repair immediately reproducible in a migration.
56	7. **Deployment is not a release:** every Vercel build has its own SWBOM. A public release additionally requires a source archive containing the same Production build's SWBOM and the complete GPL license.
57	8. **Landing-page data is public by design:** expose only an explicit, approved read model for leaderboard and discoverable lobby metadata. A landing-page query is never a shortcut to the private room API.
58	
59	Vercel and Supabase plans, quotas, CLI behavior, and terms can change. This plan records a baseline checked on 26 October 2026 and requires a fresh official-doc/account-dashboard check before provisioning and each release. The values below are planning constraints, not a guarantee of future quotas.
60	
61	## 3. Environments and data boundaries
62	
63	| Environment | Hosting and branch | Database | Data and access rules |
64	|---|---|---|---|
65	| **Development** | Local Next.js server; local Supabase stack where the developer has a compatible container runtime. | Local disposable database; deterministic seeded content. | Mocked external services for unit/component tests; no Production data or credentials. `.env.local` and `.vercel/` are ignored by Git. |
66	| **Staging** | Persistent non-production branch (proposed name: `staging`) deploys to Vercel Preview. | Dedicated Supabase Free project. | Synthetic profiles, rooms, content, and test sessions only. Protect the Preview URL with Vercel's available deployment protection; reviewer access is explicitly granted. |
67	| **Feature Preview** | Each non-production branch/PR receives an immutable Vercel Preview URL. | Default to the Staging Supabase project with per-test unique identifiers; allow a branch-specific override only when a separately approved free project exists. | No Production secrets/data. Use branch-specific Vercel Preview variables to target `staging`; feature branches inherit the safe Preview defaults. Ensure tests clean up only their own seeded rows. |
68	| **Production** | Vercel Production deployments from `main`. | Dedicated Production Supabase Free project. | Real users/data; least-privilege keys; change control and release verification. Never use this environment for automated acceptance or destructive tests. |
69	
70	Vercel Hobby currently provides Local, Preview, and Production environments; named custom environments are documented for Pro/Enterprise. Therefore “Staging” is a persistent protected Preview branch and isolated Supabase project, not a paid custom Vercel environment. Branch-specific Preview variables allow that branch to use its staging database while other Preview deployments inherit the non-production default. Local Supabase development is free but requires a Docker API-compatible container runtime; if unavailable, use mock-backed tests and do integration checks in Staging with strictly synthetic data.
71	
72	Supabase Free currently permits two free projects across an owner's/admin's organizations. Allocate those projects to Staging and Production; confirm account availability before provisioning. Do not create a new hosted Supabase project for each branch. Make branch previews data-safe through opaque test prefixes, short-lived fixtures, cleanup scoped to the fixture owner, and no assumption that the shared staging database is empty.
73	
74	## 4. Provisioning plan
75	
76	### Administration configuration
77	
78	Apply migration `010_access_control.sql` before using the [administration/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md). Set `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` only in the server environment to a comma-separated list of existing profile IDs. The authenticated profile panel shows the current ID. Never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for this setting and never set it from browser input. Restart/redeploy when changing the allowlist. An empty value grants no bootstrap authority; there is no default administrator account or password. Persisted grants can then be managed at `/admin/users` by an effective administrator. Use durable signed-in profiles for operational administrators; losing guest browser data loses access to that guest identity. Separate Preview and Production administrator lists and databases.
79	
80	### 4.1 Preconditions
81	
82	- Confirm repository visibility, owner, production branch (`main`), expected commit author, and Vercel Hobby eligibility.
83	- Confirm the Vercel account/team and Supabase account have access to the personal GitHub repository and room for two Free projects.
84	- Review current official plan terms, usage quotas, project pausing, log retention, database backup availability, region choice, and CLI versions.
85	- Choose a region based on expected player geography and service availability; record the choice. Avoid claiming a multi-region or uptime guarantee on Free.
86	- Approve secret names and ownership without writing secret values to this plan or the repository.
87	- Approve database schema and migrations in accordance with the implementation plan. Deployment planning may be completed during Phase 0. Provisioning, deployment tooling, and deployment execution begin only after coding Phases 1–6 are complete, in Phase 7. Confirm branch/project topology at Phase 7 deployment entry.
88	
89	### 4.2 Repeatable provisioning command
90	
91	Implement one manually invoked PowerShell provisioning entry point, backed by pinned Supabase CLI and Vercel CLI versions. The current schema planner is `scripts/hosting-schema.ps1`; the earlier Node fallback is retired. Declare tools as direct development/build dependencies or provide a pinned documented installation mechanism, and add their purpose, license, and upstream source to `ATTRIBUTIONS.md`. Final branch/project topology and account-capacity confirmation are Phase 7 deployment-entry decisions after coding, not Phase 0 exit gates.
92	
93	The command has explicit subcommands, a safe default dry-run/plan mode, and confirmation for destructive changes:
94	
95	1. `doctor`: report CLI versions, linked accounts/project IDs, repository/branch, and required variable *names*; never print token or secret values.
96	2. `plan`: show the intended project/environment/migration/variable actions without mutation. Fail if the selected project plan is not Free, if a target project is ambiguous, or if an action could point Preview at Production.
97	3. `provision staging`: create or link the Staging Supabase project and Vercel project configuration; apply approved migrations; set only Preview variables, using a branch-specific override for `staging`; verify the settings without echoing values.
98	4. `provision production`: create or link the Production Supabase project; apply the same migration sequence after Staging validation; set only Production variables; require an explicit operator confirmation and verify the target project ID before applying.
99	5. `status`: show project IDs, regions, plan names, migration version, deployment branch mapping, and secret variable names/presence only.
100	6. `backup` / `restore-check`: create a database export to an operator-controlled encrypted location, record checksum and schema version, and restore it to a disposable local/Staging database to prove recoverability. Never commit dumps or retain them in a public artifact.
101	
102	The script obtains authentication from the operator's CLI session or environment. It must redact command output, avoid shell tracing of secrets, avoid placing credentials in command-line arguments where process listings may expose them, enforce restrictive file permissions on temporary files, and remove temporary files on success/failure. It is idempotent: reruns report already-correct state and do not reset projects or erase data. No script may silently change a plan or enable a paid feature.
103	
104	### 4.3 Infrastructure configuration under version control
105	
106	Store Supabase configuration, SQL migrations, seed fixtures, application build commands, and non-secret environment-variable names in the repo. Store no access token, database password, service-role key, OAuth client secret, user data, or exported database. Keep environment configuration as an allowlisted schema describing required key, target environments, public/private classification, and validation rule.
107	
108	Use a two-person review where possible; otherwise use an explicit self-review checklist for Production. Supabase schema and RLS policies are reviewed as code. Keep Vercel build configuration in the project files only where the framework actually requires it; do not duplicate settings in incompatible Dashboard and file-based configuration.
109	
110	## 5. Git-to-Vercel workflow (post-coding phase)
111	
112	Do not connect the repository to Vercel or execute deployments during coding Phases 1–6. Complete local and disposable-service validation first. Begin this workflow only in Phase 7, after the coding phase is complete and the full AC suite passes.
113	
114	### 5.1 Repository setup
115	
116	1. Connect the existing `sharpninja/wordpairs` repository to a Vercel Hobby project owned by the matching personal Vercel account.
117	2. Select the production branch `main`; verify the framework preset, root directory, install command, test/build command, and output handling from the implemented Next.js app.
118	3. Enable deployment comments/links where available. Review fork deployment authorization and Preview protection so an untrusted pull request cannot access secrets or run against Production.
119	4. Add Preview and Production environment variables with least privilege. Apply a branch-specific Preview override for `staging`; Preview defaults still point only to Staging/non-production infrastructure.
120	5. Enable Vercel-provided environment metadata needed by the build (commit SHA, branch, deployment URL/environment). Treat all build-time environment values as secrets unless explicitly classified as public.
121	6. Verify one feature branch Preview and one `main` Production deployment. Confirm the author rule and that no GitHub Actions workflow is involved.
122	7. Verify the anonymous landing-page route is reachable without authentication and returns only the public projection; inspect rendered HTML, network responses, cache headers, logs, and the SWBOM endpoint for accidental secrets or private lobby/game fields.
123	
124	### 5.2 Normal change path
125	
126	1. Start from current `main`; create a short-lived feature branch named for the work item and AC IDs.
127	2. Before implementation, pass the increment's mock-first TDD gate. The build cannot proceed if tests fail.
128	3. Push the branch. Vercel automatically builds a Preview. The build sequence is: install from lockfile → static/type/content checks → full test suite → generate and validate deployment SWBOM → production framework build including the SWBOM.
129	4. Validate the Preview URL, environment label, branch, commit, database target, and SWBOM endpoint. Execute acceptance/browser tests against synthetic staging data; review accessibility and log/errors.
130	5. Merge only after review and all gates. Vercel deploys the new `main` commit to Production. Migration ordering must be safe for old and new application revisions during rollout.
131	6. Run a post-deploy smoke checklist against the immutable Production deployment URL and canonical domain; inspect errors and quota dashboard. Do not run destructive tests against Production.
132	
133	### 5.3 Build command and gates
134	
135	The eventual package scripts should make the sequence explicit and exit non-zero on any failed gate. Exact command names are selected after dependency versions are validated and pinned.
136	
137	| Gate | Required checks | Failure behavior |
138	|---|---|---|
139	| Source | Clean lockfile install; type/lint/static analysis; curated content validation; verify generated files are deterministic. | Stop build. |
140	| Tests | Unit/component and all earlier increment suites; acceptance traceability report confirms all active ACs have tests; mock-first result is recorded. | Stop before SBOM/application build. |
141	| Supply-chain | Generate CycloneDX JSON 1.6 from the exact lockfile; include runtime and development/build dependencies and required metadata; validate schema, commit SHA, environment, deployment URL, and absence of secrets. | Stop build; do not deploy an artifact with missing or wrong metadata. |
142	| Application | Next.js production build; include report at `public/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`; verify exact endpoint path is part of output. | Vercel deployment fails. |
143	| Deployment | Verify Vercel environment and source commit; check expected Supabase project binding; run smoke checks, including anonymous landing-page and public-data privacy checks. | Do not promote/announce release; use rollback procedure if Production is degraded. |
144	
145	Every successful Preview and Production deployment serves its own immutable `/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`. Include the Vercel deployment URL, `VERCEL_ENV`, branch and commit metadata available at build time. Ensure metadata is escaped/validated and does not disclose environment variables. Preview and Production deployments from the same SHA still have distinct build/deployment metadata and each report belongs to the URL that serves it.
146	
147	## 6. Database migration and change strategy
148	
149	- Develop each migration locally or against a disposable database; run schema and RLS tests against mocks first, then the Supabase local stack or Staging.
150	- Keep migrations forward-compatible across the currently deployed and candidate application versions. Prefer expand → deploy compatible code → migrate/backfill → contract in later work. Do not drop/rename a live column in the same release that first stops reading it.
151	- Apply the same ordered migration set to Staging, then Production. Verify migration history/version before and after. A production migration command requires the selected project ID to match an allowlisted Production ID and a human confirmation.
152	- Seed only curated public content through reviewed, idempotent migration/seed files. Keep synthetic test accounts separate from real user data.
153	- Define transaction and lock behavior for online changes. Estimate table size and lock duration before applying any expensive migration under the Free database resource limit.
154	- Supabase Free currently lists a 500 MB database per project, 5 GB egress, 200 Realtime peak connections, 2 million Realtime messages/month, and pausing after a week of low activity; its pricing page also lists no automatic backups. The requirements additionally set 100 Realtime messages/second as an operating threshold. Treat all of these as hard ceilings and verify the live project dashboard before deployment; design a buffer below each ceiling and test the recoverable quota response.
155	- Because free automatic backups are not included in the current plan, operator-managed encrypted exports and restore drills are required before real user data is accepted. These exports are disaster-recovery copies, not releases, and must not be placed in GitHub, Vercel static output, or public artifacts.
156	
157	## 7. Observability and incident response
158	
159	### Signals to inspect
160	
161	- Vercel deployment status, build duration/failure, function errors/duration/invocation quotas, runtime logs, and current Hobby usage.
162	- Supabase project status/paused state, database/storage size, egress, Realtime concurrent connections/messages, authentication errors, migration history, and available logs/retention.
163	- Landing-page read-model health: leaderboard query age, discoverable/joinable lobby result count, empty-state rate, cache age, query errors, and public projection field allowlist. Do not log individual leaderboard identities beyond the approved operational need.
164	- Application-level counters: active rooms/players/observers, join failures, readiness timeouts, reconnect rates, state-transition conflicts, quota responses, and repeated client retries. Collect the minimum data needed; do not log raw guesses, tokens, secret values, or unnecessary identity data.
165	- SWBOM endpoint reachability and commit/deployment metadata for each deployment.
166	
167	Since the Free plans do not promise a production SLA and have limited log retention, the runbook relies on operator review and exported deployment evidence. Alerting must not create a paid external dependency. Establish user-facing status copy for service unavailable, capacity reached, maintenance, and paused Supabase project states.
168	
169	### Incident sequence
170	
171	1. Identify affected environment, commit SHA, and service status; preserve relevant non-sensitive logs and quota snapshots.
172	2. Stop further migrations/releases if data integrity or auth is uncertain. Never enable paid usage to recover service.
173	3. For a bad application deployment, redeploy/rollback to the last known-good immutable Vercel deployment using the Vercel-supported rollback/promotion mechanism; verify it points to a compatible schema.
174	4. For schema/data faults, use a reviewed forward repair migration or restore a verified encrypted export to a deliberate recovery target. Do not assume a Vercel code rollback reverses database changes.
175	5. For a quota or project pause, show recoverable status, follow the current Free-plan resume/quota instructions, and validate data integrity before reopening joins. Do not repeatedly issue requests that increase quota pressure.
176	6. Record impact, timeline, root cause, data-loss assessment, recovery actions, and prevention work in a private incident log; update this plan and relevant tests/ACs.
177	
178	## 8. Release and archive procedure
179	
180	1. Select a Production deployment with known commit SHA `S` and verify it passed all tests and post-deploy checks.
181	2. Retrieve the SWBOM from that exact deployment's `/sbom/S.cdx.json`; validate JSON/CycloneDX 1.6, build/deployment URL, branch, lockfile inventory, commit SHA, license inventory, and no-secret scan.
182	3. Check out the corresponding source tag/commit and build a source archive reproducibly. Include all source needed to modify/build the release, root `LICENSE`, `ATTRIBUTIONS.md`, required third-party notices, release metadata, and the exact SWBOM at `sbom/S.cdx.json`.
183	4. Exclude `.env*`, `.vercel/`, Supabase access tokens, local database files/dumps, cached credentials, and unrelated generated artifacts. Include project source/configuration and migrations needed to reproduce the release.
184	5. Inspect the archive listing and extract it to a clean temporary directory. Confirm one `LICENSE`, one matching report, expected SHA, and no secret-like files; rerun the archive validation against the extracted contents.
185	6. Publish the archive and checksum through the approved GitHub release method. No GitHub Actions asset generation is involved; the operator manually invokes the versioned packaging command and reviews its output.
186	7. Open the release archive after publication, compare its checksum to the local validated archive, download/extract it, and verify the SWBOM and GPL notice are present.
187	
188	The packaging script must be deterministic where practical: stable file ordering, normalized timestamps/ownership, and checksum recorded separately. It must fail closed on missing/malformed/mismatched SWBOM or license review. The Production build artifact and source tag must identify the same commit; never attach a newer SWBOM to an older source archive.
189	
190	## 9. Rollback and recovery objectives
191	
192	During Phase 0, set realistic recovery-time and recovery-point expectations suitable for the game and free plans. The following are proposed controls, not uptime guarantees:
193	
194	- **Application rollback:** keep the prior known-good Vercel deployment available; rollback code without changing database configuration. Validate current schema compatibility before rollback.
195	- **Database recovery:** establish an encrypted operator-held backup/export cadence and retention window before onboarding real users; prove restoration to Staging/local and document the expected data-loss window. Supabase Free lacks automatic backups according to the current pricing table, so no managed point-in-time recovery is assumed.
196	- **Secrets:** rotate compromised credentials in the provider dashboard/CLI, update only affected environment scopes, redeploy, then verify that old credentials are rejected. Do not place secret values in issue comments or logs.
197	- **Project pause:** maintain a documented resume procedure and owner contact path for the Supabase project. Reopening after pause requires database connection, migration status, auth, and Realtime smoke checks.
198	
199	## 10. Deployment acceptance checklist
200	
201	### Provisioning and security
202	
203	- [ ] Vercel Hobby use remains personal/non-commercial; repository owner and commit author comply with current Hobby Git rules.
204	- [ ] Supabase Staging and Production are separate Free projects; no third paid resource is configured.
205	- [ ] Environment variables are scoped correctly; Preview cannot reach Production; secrets are absent from Git, logs, static files, artifacts, and screenshots.
206	- [ ] Provisioning `plan` is non-mutating; rerun is idempotent; production apply is target-checked and confirmed; migrations match the reviewed source.
207	- [ ] Staging and Production recovery procedures and encrypted backup/restore check are documented.
208	
209	### Build and deployment
210	
211	- [ ] A feature branch gets a Preview; `main` gets Production; no GitHub Actions workflow is required.
212	- [ ] Build order runs checks/tests before SWBOM and app build; failed tests fail deployment.
213	- [ ] Preview uses Staging credentials; Production uses Production credentials; protected fork deployment cannot expose secrets.
214	- [ ] TR-27 operational check confirms each deployment serves the SWBOM for its exact commit, lockfile, environment, and URL without secret values; this is TR evidence, not AC coverage.
215	- [ ] Smoke checks confirm the anonymous landing page, approved leaderboard projection, discoverable/joinable lobby summary, rules content, identity, room creation/join, quota error handling, and expected environment labeling.
216	- [ ] AC-43 and AC-50 contract tests pass against local components with mocked public projections before implementation. Any deployed smoke check is diagnostic only and does not count toward AC coverage.
217	- [ ] TR-23/TR-26/TR-27 configuration, provisioning, build-gate, and SWBOM checks pass as TR-only evidence; they do not substitute for AC coverage.
218	
219	### Release archive
220	
221	- [ ] Source release archive contains the complete corresponding source, `LICENSE`, attribution notices, and the SWBOM from the matching Production deployment.
222	- [ ] Archive SWBOM SHA equals the source release SHA; archive listing/extraction and secret scan pass.
223	- [ ] Published archive checksum matches the validated local artifact; the release is manually verified after publication.

240	The local Realtime gateway, independent scheduler and real browser integration are documented in [the live multiplayer extension](room_sync_fix.md). This temporary leased runtime preserves the game database and is not a Vercel/Supabase cloud deployment. A cloud deployment must provide an independent deadline/outbox trigger and verify actual private delivery before release; browser polling does not establish scheduler health.
